topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out its core learning objectives.

topics.label: Traditional cancer interventions and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore conventional therapeutic approaches including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic cytotoxic agents alongside their toxicities and resistance pathways.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific dependencies and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of targeted drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the targeting of oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and examine the structural, bypass, and paradoxical resistance mechanisms that emerge during treatment.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are deployed to target cancer cell surface proteins selectively.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and the development of therapeutic modalities that reactivate or engineer T cells against malignancies.

topics.label: Therapeutic progress, systemic challenges, and future paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad clinical challenges, historical treatment outcomes, and future considerations for managing cancer heterogeneity and patient care.
